## Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts` → `migrateAuthToAuthJson()` parsed the legacy file with `JSON.parse(readFileSync(oauthPath, "utf-8"))` — no BOM handling, unlike every other JSON reader in the package (all use `stripBom`). A legacy `oauth.json` written with a UTF-8 BOM therefore threw inside the swallowing `try/catch`: no provider migrated, `oauth.json` never renamed, and settings.json `apiKeys` quietly won instead of the OAuth credential.

## Change (minimal, 1 line of production code)

```ts
const oauth = JSON.parse(stripBom(readFileSync(oauthPath, "utf-8")));
```

`stripBom` was already imported and used for `settings.json` and `keybindings.json`. Nothing else moved, so all named invariants are unchanged: apiKey fallback for providers without OAuth, OAuth precedence per provider, malformed files still skipped before `renameSync` (never destroyed), `oauth.json.migrated` keeps original bytes, and an existing `auth.json` still short-circuits everything.

Temp dirs are removed in a `finally`.
